g.text: AAuth PS Authorization Access (Three-Party)
Person
Agent
Agent Provider
Person Server
Resource
Agent Token (identity)
Person Token (who the agent acts for)
Resource Token (what the resource requires)
Auth Token (consent)
Signed Resource Access
Prove key possession (platform specific, see AAuth Bootstrap)
agent token (aa-agent+jwt) with cnf = agent key and ps = person server URL
POST person_token_endpoint with resource = URL, HTTP Sig with agent token
First use of this resource? Show its metadata and ask (202 interaction, or a tap out of band)
Approve
person token (aa-person+jwt) with aud = resource, directed sub, cnf = agent key
POST authorization_endpoint, or any call, HTTP Sig with person token
401 or 200 with resource token (aa-resource+jwt) with aud = PS, ps, sub, presented_jti, scope
POST auth_token_endpoint with resource_token and presented_token, HTTP Sig with agent token
Consent card = resource metadata, resource-asserted scope, agent-asserted justification (202 interaction)
Approve, deny, or ask the agent a clarification
auth token (aa-auth+jwt) with aud = resource, ps, sub, scope, cnf = agent key
GET /api with Signature-Key sig=jwt and HTTP Message Signature
Verify signature, cnf matches signing key, aud, and the (iss, sub) record
200 OK
Portable identity. Verifiable by any resource from the agent provider's JWKS, with no registration at the resource.
⚠️ SECURITY: Identity only, no scope. The sub is directed per resource, so resources cannot correlate the person.
The resource, not the client, authors and signs the authorization request. OAuth has no equivalent.
Pending is a state, not an error. The agent polls the pending URL while the person decides.
⚠️ SECURITY: Never bearer. A stolen token is useless without the agent's private key.
